name: default-packages-pinning-policy
description: Pinning policy for language dependencies and CI actions. Scanners are policy-agnostic; everything opinionated lives here.
_npm_registry_note: Any .npmrc registry= or @scope:registry= pointing elsewhere is a dependency-confusion surface, not necessarily malicious - flagged for review, not auto-condemned.

priority_rules.why: unpinned reference in a release/publish workflow - can change what the next tag ships
priority_rules._content_contains_any_note: Matched against path+content combined, lowercase - catches both a workflow named release.yml and one merely triggered `on: release:` inside an otherwise generic filename.

_priority_note: Ordered; first match wins. Matches the spec's model: P0 = executes in CI with credentials or affects a published artifact; P1 = developer machines and build time; P2 = documentation, examples, demos, dead repositories.
_archived_note: The correct fix for an archived repo is usually archiving harder - deleting it - not editing it.
_self_exclude_note: A scanner's own fixtures legitimately contain every pattern it hunts for. Exclusions are COUNTED and listed in the report - a silent exclusion is how a real finding disappears.
_known_action_orgs_note: Not a static acceptability signal (any of these can still be unpinned) - only used to keep the self-test's fixture noise-free. Ownership (personal-account / archived-upstream) is a --resolve-only network check (D1); this list has no bearing on it.

known_benign_collisions._value_note: npm's own local/workspace protocol specifiers (file:, link:, workspace:) are not registry ranges and are never a mutability finding - the referenced path is version-controlled alongside the manifest.
